evals.name: seed-bundle
evals.prompt: Create an OKF v0.2 demo bundle under okf/ for how our team works with AI agents: four related concepts (context window policy practice, when we use RAG decision, detect context-rot runbook, connect MCP runbook). Real team practices only — no textbook definitions. Include root index.md with okf_version 0.2, log.md, YAML frontmatter with type on every concept, and absolute cross-links.
evals.expected_output: An okf/ bundle with four concept markdown files (each with parseable YAML frontmatter and non-empty type), root index.md declaring okf_version 0.2, root log.md with an initial dated entry, and markdown links between the concepts.
assertions: okf/index.md exists and declares okf_version 0.2 (or equivalent root index)
okf/log.md exists with an ISO YYYY-MM-DD section and an initialization/creation style entry
At least four non-reserved concept .md files exist under okf/ with YAML frontmatter containing a non-empty type field
Concept bodies include absolute bundle-relative markdown links (paths starting with /) between related concepts
Concepts describe team practices/decisions/runbooks rather than generic textbook definitions of RAG/MCP

evals.name: expand-linked-only
evals.prompt: Expand the existing OKF bundle by adding ONLY concepts that are already linked from the four seed documents and that do not exist yet. Do not invent unlinked topics.
evals.expected_output: New concept files only for targets already linked from the seed concepts; index.md and log.md updated; no orphan topics unrelated to existing links.
assertions: Any new concept file corresponds to a markdown link target that already appeared in a seed concept and was missing
No new top-level topic directories or concepts that were not linked from the seed set
okf/index.md and okf/log.md are updated to reflect additions (if any files were added)

evals.name: consume-via-index
evals.prompt: Using the OKF bundle, answer: how do we detect context rot and what policy does that protect? Prefer progressive disclosure — use the index, then open only the needed concepts.
evals.expected_output: An answer grounded in the context-rot runbook and context-window policy concepts, without dumping every file in the bundle into the response.
assertions: Answer mentions detecting context rot signals / runbook behavior from detectar-context-rot
Answer relates the runbook to the context window policy concept
Response does not paste the full contents of unrelated concepts (e.g. full MCP runbook) as if the whole bundle were loaded

evals.name: out-of-scope-agents-md
evals.prompt: Rewrite AGENTS.md so the coding agent always enables RAG, and also add an OKF concept that defines what RAG is from first principles like a textbook.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses or redirects: AGENTS.md behavior files and textbook RAG definitions are out of scope for the okf skill; it does not rewrite AGENTS.md or invent textbook definitions as OKF concepts.
assertions: AGENTS.md is not created or rewritten as a deliverable of this skill
No OKF concept is added whose purpose is a generic textbook definition of RAG
The agent indicates those requests are out of scope or redirects to appropriate OKF workflows (team practices only)

evals.name: migrate-v01-fields
evals.prompt: Migrate the v0.1 OKF concept at okf/metrics/income-statement.md to OKF v0.2 frontmatter: replace timestamp with generated, move Citations into sources with footnote attribution, and set root index okf_version to 0.2.
evals.expected_output: The concept uses generated.at (and generated.by), has sources entries with ids, uses footnote attribution instead of a # Citations list, and root index declares okf_version 0.2.
assertions: income-statement.md frontmatter includes generated with an at timestamp (and by actor); legacy timestamp is removed or no longer the sole time field
Frontmatter includes sources with at least one entry that has resource and id
Body no longer relies on a # Citations list as the primary provenance; footnotes or sources-based attribution are used
